subject: Designing and extending an application exception-reporting pipeline — error-boundary placement, tracker-SDK wrappers,…

evals.prompt: Define error-tracking in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the error-tracking skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind error-tracking. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "design accessible error-message copy and recovery UI for the 404 page". Should error-tracking activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force error-tracking onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to refactor, debugging, owasp-security, a11y, code-review, testing-strategy, error-boundary.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "set up exception reporting for a new React + Next.js application". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying error-tracking.
Place error-tracking among its adjacent skills (refactor, debugging, owasp-security, a11y, code-review, testing-strategy, error-boundary). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about error-tracking and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
